security.anonymous.about: With anonymous access, people and clients can browse and download repository content without signing in. The permissions of the anonymous user decide which content they can reach.
security.anonymous.enabled: Let anonymous users access the server
security.anonymous.enabledText: Turn on anonymous access to repository content
security.anonymous.intro: Set up access for users who do not sign in
security.anonymous.realmHint: The security realm that anonymous callers are authenticated in
security.anonymous.sectionText: When this is on, callers who do not sign in can reach content, limited to what the anonymous user account is allowed to do.
security.anonymous.title: Anonymous Access
security.anonymous.userIdHint: The user that anonymous access runs as
security.filters.automatic: Filters take effect as you pick them
security.filters.title: Filters
security.form.emailRule: Enter an address such as jane@example.org
security.form.idSpaces: Must not start or end with a space
security.form.nameRule: Use letters, digits, hyphens, underscores and dots; start with a letter, digit or hyphen
security.password.description: The user signs in with the new password from now on. Their other sessions end.
security.password.title: Change the password of {id}
security.privilege.applicationActionsHel: What may be done in this domain. As a list: separated by commas (for example, read,edit)
security.privilege.descriptionHelp: A short note on what the privilege allows (for example, "Lets people browse every Maven repository")
security.privilege.domainHelp: The part of the server the privilege covers. Pick a suggestion or type your own (for example, tasks)
security.privilege.formatHelp: The format of the repositories the privilege applies to. * means all formats (for example, maven2)
security.privilege.nameHelp: A unique name of letters, digits, dashes and underscores (for example, repository-view-maven)
security.privilege.patternHelp: Parts are separated by colons and values by commas; * stands for anything, as in astrum:repository-view:maven2:*:read.
security.privilege.repositoryActionsHelp: What may be done with the settings or the content. As a list: separated by commas (for example, browse,read)
security.privilege.repositoryHelp: The repository the privilege applies to. * means all repositories (for example, maven-releases)
security.privilege.scopeChoose: Pick a format and a repository to see the content.
security.privilege.scopeRepository: The privilege covers what the selector picks in {repository}.
security.privilege.selectorActionsHelp: What may be done with the content. As a list: separated by commas (for example, read,browse)
security.privilege.selectorHelp: The CSEL expression of the selector limits the paths the privilege covers.
security.privilege.selectorRepositoryHel: The repository the privilege applies to. * means all repositories (for example, npm-all)
security.privilege.stepType: Step 1: pick the type of the privilege
security.privilegeField.name: Name
security.privilegeProfile.api: API endpoints that need this permission
security.privilegeProfile.openRole: Open the profile of the role {name}
security.privilegeType.applicationText: A permission for one part of the application
security.privilegeType.repositoryAdminTe: Control over the settings of repositories
security.privilegeType.repositoryContent: Access limited by the expression of a content selector
security.privilegeType.repositoryViewTex: Browse, read and change the content of repositories
security.privilegeType.wildcardText: A privilege written as a pattern
security.privileges.deleteText: Roles that grant it lose it. This cannot be undone.
security.privileges.helpText: A privilege opens one operation or one resource of Astrum Repository. Roles collect privileges and users receive roles, and that decides what each user can do.
security.privileges.intro: Manage privileges and the permissions they grant
security.privileges.name: Name
security.privileges.search: Find privileges by name, description or permission…
security.privileges.title: Privileges
security.realms.about: Security realms check who is calling the server. The active realms are asked one after another in the order shown. Move realms between the Available and Active lists, and drag the active ones to change their order.
security.realms.intro: The security realms in use and the order the server asks them in
security.realms.localText: Without the local users realm nobody with a local account can sign in, the administrator included. Make sure another realm lets you in before you save.
security.realms.noneActive: Keep at least one realm active
security.realms.title: Realms
security.role.descriptionHelp: An optional note on what the role is for
security.role.idHelp: A unique identifier of the role
security.role.mappedRoleHint: Enter or search for a role from {source}. Type 3+ characters to search.
security.role.mappedRoleNone: Nothing found. You can still save the mapping: it takes effect once {source} has a group with this name.
security.role.nameHelp: A readable name of the role
security.role.privilegesIntro: Find and pick the privileges to grant. Results are grouped by kind.
security.role.rolesIntro: Pick the roles this role contains. It inherits their privileges.
security.role.sourceHint: Select the external authentication source (LDAP or OpenID Connect)
security.role.typeHint: Select whether this is a standard Astrum role or maps to an external authentication source
security.role.typeIntro: Pick what kind of role to create.
security.roleProfile.effectiveIntro: Every privilege this role grants, directly or through the roles it contains, in one list.
security.roleProfile.intro: What the role grants and whom it reaches
security.roleProfile.usersIntro: Users who have the role {id} assigned directly.
security.roles.deleteText: Users and roles that hold it lose it. This cannot be undone.
security.roles.helpText: A role is a set of privileges that together make up permissions. The roles of a user decide what the user may do in Astrum Repository, and a role may contain other roles to build a hierarchy.
security.roles.intro: Manage roles and the privileges they grant
security.roles.name: Name
security.roles.search: Find roles by name, ID or description…
security.roles.title: Roles
security.ssrf.badDomain: {value} is not a domain name such as registry.local or *.corp.example
security.ssrf.badIp: {value} is not an IP address or a network such as 10.0.0.0/8
security.ssrf.domainsHint: Host names that may resolve to internal addresses. *.example.org also allows every subdomain.
security.ssrf.enabledText: Proxy repositories and other outgoing requests may not reach loopback, private, link-local or other internal addresses, unless they are allowed below.
security.ssrf.intro: Keep outgoing requests of the server away from internal networks
security.ssrf.ipsHint: Single addresses such as 192.168.1.10, or networks such as 10.0.0.0/8 and fd00::/8
security.ssrf.offWarning: With the protection off, anyone who may configure a proxy repository can make the server call internal services.
security.ssrf.title: SSRF protection
security.tree.name: Name
security.user.editIntro: Change the profile, the roles and see the effective permissions of the user.
security.user.firstNameHelp: The first name shown for the user
security.user.lastNameHelp: The last name shown for the user
security.user.notFound: There is no user {id} in this source
security.user.passwordHelp: The first password. The user can change it later.
security.user.toggleStatus: Switch the status of the user (now: {status})
security.user.treeEmpty: Grant at least one role to see the effective permissions.
security.users.deleteText: Their sessions end and their access tokens are deleted. This cannot be undone.
security.users.helpText: Users are the people and systems that work with Astrum Repository. Each user receives roles that give certain permissions. Local users are created and managed in Astrum; external users sign in through LDAP, OpenID Connect or other configured sources.
security.users.intro: Manage users and the roles they hold
security.users.name: Name
security.users.title: Users
